correctness.rationale: On an equal-height rooted tree the normalization is precisely 2H. With delta=x-y, exact edge summation reduces both metrics to the integer pair k,c with 0<=c<=k<=N-3, because every species is present in both communities. Any reversed strictly ordered comparisons force 1<=k-l<t(c-d)<=t(N-3). The explicit x=(N-2,1,1), y=(1,N-2,1), z=(2,1,N-3) realizes reversal whenever t(N-3)>1, including all endpoint strictness. The closed-integer N_min is algebraically correct. Independently implemented raw edge sums agreed with exact reduction in 10,584 ordered pairs and 218,484 common-reference candidates for N=3..9 and seven rational t values; finite checks only corroborate the all-N proof.

General tree transport identities do cover the algebraic metric formula but not the exact all-profile order classification.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A general distance formula entails computability of each comparison but does not, by itself, assert the extremal inequality t(N-3)<=1 or construct a shared-reference reversal for all t(N-3)>1. Previously reported empirical disagreements demonstrate possibility in some settings but neither the universal prohibition nor exact minimal census.

originality.rationale: The metric formulas and transport equivalence are previously known, but the exact global all-integer-census cutoff for strict order reversal, including its sharp common-reference witness and equality phase boundary, is not implied by any inspected published statement without an additional extremal integer-gap argument. See the four implication comparisons and full-text section readings. Residual unindexed theorem risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unindexed more general rank-concordance theorem for integral empirical probability measures under two tree metrics could imply this restricted exact boundary despite not mentioning the two ecological names.
The threshold is purely combinatorial for a three-tip ultrametric tree; it is not a claim about statistical confidence of inferred ecological rankings or arbitrary phylogenetic shapes.

value.rationale: Bray–Curtis and normalized weighted UniFrac are central alternative phylogenetic/nonphylogenetic beta-diversity metrics. The exact all-N phase diagram, including a universal no-reversal guarantee, the sharp integer census staircase and a matching shared-reference witness, explains when phylogeny can change the ordering of dissimilarities on the smallest nontrivial rooted species tree. This is a natural structural boundary, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a mere normalization identity; value is limited to this controlled finite-census setting.
